increments.title: Save and continue no longer waits for virus scans, and Save and return to overview keeps a typed-in document
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 saves a complete document and moves the trader on at once when they press Save and continue, even while a document is still being scanned, and applies the same check before Save and return to overview, saving a document whose type is chosen. Today Save and continue saves the document and brings the trader back to the page, any document not yet scanned clean holds them, and Save and return to overview leaves at once and drops a part-filled document. Waiting for the scan is not a constraint, because the backend only publishes documents that scanned clean, so pending scans stop holding the trader; a document the scan rejected still does.

increments.title: A document still being scanned no longer holds the trader on Upload documents
increments.detail: Today a document whose virus scan has not finished holds Save and continue: the page comes back with 'You cannot continue until all documents have been scanned or removed', so a trader who has attached everything has to wait on the page until the scan settles. After this a document still showing 'Scanning for virus' lets the trader carry on, and the page says nothing about waiting. A document the scan rejected still holds them, because that one has to be removed before the notification is right.

increments.title: Attach files up to 50MB
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 allows files up to 50MB, and DR1's inc-138 judged the same change. The backend already accepts 50MB. The frontend holds the limit at 10MB only because CDP's nginx ingress caps request bodies at 10 MiB; one limit applies in every environment, so the change waits until CDP raises that cap. Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling keeps this row blocked on that cap, tracked by EUDPA-518.
acceptanceCriteria: The Attachment size bullet reads 'files that are smaller than 50MB'. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/upload-documents.html:171; trace:prototype-dr2-1 TRACE C action 92; document:dr1-parity-backlog backlog.json inc-138)

A file of exactly 50,000,000 bytes is added and scans to 'Check completed' with no error, on the local stack and in every CDP environment. (document:dr1-parity-backlog backlog.json inc-138 finding.correction; trace:prototype-dr2-1 pet-cats-by-air action 89)

With JavaScript, choosing a file one byte over 50MB and submitting shows 'The selected file must be smaller than 50MB' in the error summary and inline on the Attachment field, and no document is added. (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/upload-documents.html:171; document:dr1-parity-backlog backlog.json inc-138 finding.frontend)

Without JavaScript, submitting a file well over 50MB redraws the page with 'The selected file must be smaller than 50MB' in the error summary and inline on the Attachment field, rather than an error page, and no document is added. (document:dr1-parity-backlog backlog.json inc-138 finding.frontend; document:dr1-parity-notes Pins, lines 211-217)
notes: Kept apart from the copy row so the wording change (req-508) is not held up by the platform blocker. The route's payload cap is the limit plus 1KiB of multipart allowance. A configurable limit was rejected by DR1 because it gives no parity anywhere. The backend needs no change: it already accepts 50MB.

One limit applies in every environment and every set: if the germinal-products documents page (req-1825) has been copied before this unblocks, this row raises its limit too, and its criteria then hold on both sets' documents pages. Plants has no file attachment (plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json).

Dropped 26 Oct: EUDPA-296 delivered it, and the blocker it waited on is gone rather than lifted. The frontend's limit is 50MB (features/documents/upload-config.js MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB = 50) and the page states 'files that are smaller than 50MB', so criterion 1 is met. The CDP request-size cap no longer stands in the way: the browser now posts the file to /upload-and-scan on the frontend's own domain, and CDP's managed nginx gives that location client_max_body_size 2304M on every service, proxied straight to cdp-uploader (docs/best-practices/node/hapi.md, from DEFRA/cdp-nginx-upstreams src/templates/server.conf.tpl). So no platform request is needed and EUDPA-518 is not on this path. Criterion 2 is proved by tests/animals/e2e/features/documents-large-uploads.spec.ts, which uploads a file of exactly 50,000,000 bytes, waits for 'Check completed' and reads the same bytes back. Criterion 3 is proved by documents-limits.spec.ts 'accepts a PDF at the maximum file size and rejects one a byte over it', which checks the summary link and the inline Attachment error and that nothing is added. Criterion 4 is proved at fit level by upload.fit.spec.js 'a file the upload service refuses as too large is reported on receipt', where the refusal comes back from the service with the browser's own size check never having fired, and is drawn on the file field with no document added. Recorded commit: animals frontend ab3ac4f0 (#424). Left over: openspec SCN-DOCS-001-A still states the limit as 10MB, which is now wrong; that is inc-039. deferred.md's row for the 50 MB limit and EUDPA-518 should be closed off with this finding.

increments.title: The Upload documents specification states the file size and reference rules the service now applies
increments.detail: EUDPA-296 rebuilt the document upload to post the file straight to the upload service, and with it raised the file size limit to 50MB and settled which characters a document reference may carry. The Behaviour Spec was not brought with it on both counts: the upload-documents specification still states the limit as 10MB, which is no longer what the page tells a trader, and it says nothing at all about the reference's characters, so a reader cannot tell a deliberate rule from an accident. A reader of the spec must be able to trust it against the running service. After this the specification states the 50MB limit the page states, and states which characters a reference may carry and what a trader is told when it carries another.
acceptanceCriteria: openspec SCN-DOCS-001-A states the maximum file size as the 50MB the page states, matching features/documents/upload-config.js. (repo:frontend upload-config.js MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB; repo:frontend features/documents/copy/copy.en.js file.smallerThan)

The upload-documents specification carries a requirement that a document reference may hold letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, full stops and forward slashes, up to one hundred characters, and that any other character is refused on the reference field with the service's own wording. (repo:frontend services/document-uploads/claim-contract.js; repo:backend accompanyingdocument/ClaimUploadRequest.java)
Every scenario added or changed carries a coverage link to a test that already proves it, and tim spec lint and tim spec gaps --none pass for the live-animals/journey-pages/upload-documents prefix.
notes: Raised by the 26 October re-analysis, not by a requirement source: it closes the two pieces of drift that re-analysis found between the upload-documents specification and the code EUDPA-296 landed. The behaviour is not in question and no service repo changes, so the row is workspace only.

The tests that prove both criteria already exist: documents-large-uploads.spec.ts uploads a file of exactly 50,000,000 bytes and reads the same bytes back, documents-limits.spec.ts accepts one at the cap and refuses one a byte over, and the frontend's controller.test.js 'documents -- what a document reference may carry' covers 125-12345675, CHEDA.GB.2026.1234567 and INV 2026/0042 and refuses REF<script>. This row writes no test; it links them.

Do not restate the character rule as 'any non-blank reference'. Design Release 2.1 asks for that, but main deliberately narrows it and tells the trader so ('Document reference must only include letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, full stops and forward slashes'). The spec records what the service does; re-opening the design question is inc-033's closing note, not this row.
